extracted.intended_audience: Parties, applicants, licensees, counsel, and Commission staff interacting with the FCC (ex parte practice, environmental filings, and RF compliance)
extracted.subtask_short: FCC ex parte and environmental compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing ex parte presentations (filing, timing, confidentiality, prohibited contacts, reporting, and sanctions) and Commission environmental review requirements (NEPA applicability, categorical exclusions, EAs/EISs, RF exposure exemptions/evaluations/mitigation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of ex parte presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting an original and one copy of the written ex parte presentation or memorandum summarizing an oral ex parte presentation to the Secretary, with a copy by mail or by electronic mail to the Commissioners or Commission employees who attended or otherwise participated in the presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Information (ex parte filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a filer believes that one or more of the documents or portions thereof to be filed should be withheld from public inspection, the filer should file electronically a request that the information not be routinely made available for public inspection pursuant to § 0.459 of this chapter. Accompanying any such request, the filer shall include in paper form a copy of the document(s) containing the confidential information, and also shall file electronically a copy of the same document(s) with the confidential information redacted. The redacted document shall be machine-readable whenever technically possible. Where the document to be filed electronically contains metadata that is confidential or protected from disclosure by a legal privilege (including, for example, the attorney-client privilege), the filer may remove such metadata from the document before filing it electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must submit both a paper (unredacted) copy with a withholding request and an electronic redacted copy; redacted copy should be machine-readable when possible; permitted to remove confidential metadata prior to electronic filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing dates outside the Sunshine period
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (b)(2)(iv) and (v) of this section, all written ex parte presentations and all summaries of oral ex parte presentations must be filed no later than two business days after the presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'business day' excludes holidays (per § 1.4(e)(1)) and for computing time limits includes the full calendar day (12:00 a.m. ET to 11:59:59 p.m. ET). Examples illustrate filing-by-end-of-day on the second business day following a presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing dates for presentations made on the day Sunshine notice is released
rubrics_metrics.description: For presentations made on the day the Sunshine notice is released, any written ex parte presentation or memorandum summarizing an oral ex parte presentation required pursuant to § 1.1206 or § 1.1208 must be submitted no later than the end of the next business day. Written replies, if any, shall be filed no later than two business days following the presentation, and shall be limited in scope to the specific issues and information presented in the ex parte filing to which they respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided (presentation on Tuesday; Sunshine agenda released same day → Sunshine period begins Wednesday → ex parte notice due end of Wednesday; reply due end of Thursday).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing dates during the Sunshine Period (exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ex parte presentation is made pursuant to an exception to the Sunshine period prohibition, the written ex parte presentation or memorandum summarizing an oral ex parte presentation required under this paragraph shall be submitted by the end of the same business day on which the ex parte presentation was made. The memorandum shall identify plainly on the first page the specific exemption in § 1.1203(a) on which the presenter relies, and shall also state the date and time at which any oral ex parte presentation was made. Written replies to permissible ex parte presentations made pursuant to an exception to the Sunshine period prohibition, if any, shall be filed no later than the next business day following the presentation, and shall be limited in scope to the specific issues and information presented in the ex parte filing to which they respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided (Sunshine period begins Wednesday; presentation on Thursday → ex parte notice due by end of Thursday; reply due by end of Friday). Memorandum must plainly state the exemption and the date/time of any oral presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of incomplete or inaccurate ex parte notices
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice of an oral ex parte presentation is incomplete or inaccurate, staff may request the filer to correct any inaccuracies or missing information. Failure by the filer to file a corrected memorandum in a timely fashion as set forth in paragraph (b) of this section, or any other evidence of substantial or repeated violations of the rules on ex parte contacts, should be reported to the General Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff can request corrections; failure to timely correct or repeated violations are reportable to the General Counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of presentations by Members of Congress and Federal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit-but-disclose proceedings involving presentations made by members of Congress or their staffs or by an agency or branch of the Federal Government or its staff shall be treated as ex parte presentations only if the presentations are of substantial significance and clearly intended to affect the ultimate decision. The Commission staff shall prepare written summaries of any such oral presentations and place them in the record in accordance with paragraph (b) of this section and also place any written presentations in the record in accordance with that paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only significant, decision-affecting presentations by government officials are treated as ex parte for recordkeeping; staff must prepare and place summaries/written presentations in the record when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of ex parte filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's Secretary shall issue a public notice listing any written ex parte presentations or written summaries of oral ex parte presentations received by his or her office relating to any permit-but-disclose proceeding. Such public notices generally should be released at least twice per week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note warns some ex parte filings not filed in accordance with requirements might not appear on the public notice; parties should review the public file to ensure awareness of all filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of ex parte presentations in restricted proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided by the Commission or its staff pursuant to § 1.1200(a) ex parte presentations (other than ex parte presentations exempt under § 1.1204(a)) to or from Commission decision-making personnel are prohibited in all proceedings not listed as exempt in § 1.1204(b) or permit-but-disclose in § 1.1206(a) until the proceeding is no longer subject to administrative reconsideration or review or judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricted proceedings include, but are not limited to, proceedings designated for hearing, amendments to broadcast allotments, Title III applications, and waiver proceedings (with specified exceptions). Presentations in restricted proceedings made on a non-ex parte basis still require filing a copy or a summary in the record consistent with § 1.1206 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-party exception in restricted proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In a restricted proceeding involving only one 'party,' as defined in § 1.1202(d), the party and the Commission may freely make presentations to each other because there is no other party to be served or with a right to have an opportunity to be present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the definition of 'party' in § 1.1202(d) to determine permissibility of presentations without service/notice and opportunity for others to be present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of restricted proceedings to permit-but-disclose
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with § 1.1200(a), the Commission or its staff may determine that a restricted proceeding not designated for hearing involves primarily issues of broadly applicable policy rather than the rights and responsibilities of specific parties and specify that the proceeding will be conducted in accordance with the provisions of § 1.1206 governing permit-but-disclose proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission/staff discretion to treat certain restricted proceedings as permit-but-disclose where policy issues predominate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on solicitation of improper presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall solicit or encourage others to make any improper presentation under the provisions of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate termination of prohibited oral presentations by Commission personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission personnel who believe that an oral presentation which is being made to them or is about to be made to them is prohibited shall promptly advise the person initiating the presentation that it is prohibited and shall terminate the discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of statements forwarded to OGC for prohibited oral presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission personnel who receive oral ex parte presentations which they believe are prohibited shall forward to the Office of General Counsel a statement containing the following information: (1) The name of the proceeding; (2) The name and address of the person making the presentation and that person's relationship (if any) to the parties to the proceeding; (3) The date and time of the presentation, its duration, and the circumstances under which it was made; (4) A full summary of the substance of the presentation; (5) Whether the person making the presentation persisted in doing so after being advised that the presentation was prohibited; and (6) The date and time that the statement was prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete, contemporaneous information must be forwarded to OGC when personnel believe an oral ex parte presentation is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of suspected prohibited written ex parte presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission personnel who receive written ex parte presentations which they believe are prohibited shall forward them to the Office of General Counsel. If the circumstances in which the presentation was made are not apparent from the presentation itself, a statement describing those circumstances shall be submitted to the Office of General Counsel with the presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and effect of prohibited presentation materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibited written ex parte presentations and all documentation relating to prohibited written and oral ex parte presentations shall be placed in a public file which shall be associated with but not made part of the record of the proceeding to which the presentations pertain. Such materials may be considered in determining the merits of a restricted proceeding only if they are made part of the record and the parties are so informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials are publicly available but are not part of the official record unless formally made so; parties must be informed if materials are incorporated into the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Counsel notification and service for prohibited presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the General Counsel determines that an ex parte presentation or presentation during the Sunshine period is prohibited by this subpart, he or she shall notify the parties to the proceeding that a prohibited presentation has occurred and shall serve on the parties copies of the presentation (if written) and any statements describing the circumstances of the presentation. Service by the General Counsel shall not be deemed to cure any violation of the rules against prohibited ex parte presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service and notification are procedural steps and do not retroactively cure violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice alternative for notification when service is unduly burdensome
rubrics_metrics.description: If the General Counsel determines that service on the parties would be unduly burdensome because the parties to the proceeding are numerous, he or she may issue a public notice in lieu of service. The public notice shall state that a prohibited presentation has been made and may also state that the presentation and related materials are available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to file sworn declaration after GC statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Counsel shall forward a copy of any statement describing the circumstances in which the prohibited ex parte presentation was made to the person who made the presentation. Within ten days thereafter, the person who made the presentation may file with the General Counsel a sworn declaration regarding the presentation and the circumstances in which it was made. The General Counsel may serve copies of the sworn declaration on the parties to the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a limited opportunity for the presenter to respond under oath; GC may circulate the response to parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of substantial public correspondence in restricted proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a restricted proceeding precipitates a substantial amount of correspondence from the general public, the procedures in paragraphs (c) through (g) of this section will not be followed with respect to such correspondence. The correspondence will be placed in a public file and be made available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mass public correspondence is treated differently (placed in public file) rather than routed through OGC procedures for prohibited presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose suspected violations to OGC
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party to a proceeding or any Commission employee who has substantial reason to believe that any violation of this subpart has been solicited, attempted, or committed shall promptly advise the Office of General Counsel in writing of all the facts and circumstances which are known to him or her.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for violations of ex parte rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon notice and hearing, any party to a proceeding who directly or indirectly violates or causes the violation of any provision of this subpart, or who fails to report the facts and circumstances concerning any such violation as required by this subpart, may be subject to sanctions as provided in paragraph (d) of this section, or disqualified from further participation in that proceeding. Commission personnel who violate provisions of this subpart may be subject to appropriate disciplinary or other remedial action as provided in part 19 of this chapter. Such sanctions as may be appropriate under the circumstances shall be imposed upon other persons who violate the provisions of this subpart. Penalties include admonishment, monetary forfeiture, or having his or her claim or interest in the proceeding dismissed, denied, disregarded, or otherwise adversely affected. The Enforcement Bureau has delegated authority to impose sanctions in such matters upon referral from the General Counsel pursuant to § 0.111(a)(15) of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions may include procedural disqualification, dismissal of claims, monetary forfeiture, and personnel disciplinary actions; referral and delegated enforcement processes apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of NEPA Subpart (applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this subpart shall apply to all Commission actions that may or will have a significant impact on the quality of the human environment. To the extent that other provisions of the Commission's rules and regulations are inconsistent with the subpart, the provisions of this subpart shall govern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEPA implementation rules here govern any conflicting Commission rules for actions with potential significant environmental impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information, assistance, and waiver of electronic filing (NEPA submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions relating to this subpart shall be made electronically. If an interested party is unable to submit or serve a filing electronically, or if it would be unreasonably burdensome to do so, such party may submit its filing on paper to the appropriate address for the Commission Secretary and serve the filing on other parties by mail. Such party should include as part of its paper submission a request for waiver of the electronic filing requirement. Such waiver request must contain an explanation addressing the requestor's inability to file electronically or why electronic filing would be unreasonably burdensome. Either showing will be sufficient to obtain a waiver under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Office of General Counsel for general information and the responsible Bureau for specific application processing; telephone provided in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS requirement for actions with significant environmental effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Commission action deemed to have a significant effect upon the quality of the human environment requires the preparation of a Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS) and Final Environmental Impact Statement (FEIS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission has found no common pattern allowing automatic specification of actions that will require EISs; applicants should consult § 1.1307 and related provisions to determine applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical exclusions from environmental processing (§1.1306)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission actions not covered by § 1.1307(a) and (b) are deemed individually and cumulatively to have no significant effect on the quality of the human environment and are categorically excluded from environmental processing. Specifically, any Commission action with respect to any new application, or minor or major modifications of existing or authorized facilities or equipment, will be categorically excluded, provided such proposals do not: (1) Involve a site location specified under § 1.1307(a)(1)-(7); or (2) Involve high intensity lighting under § 1.1307(a)(8); (3) Result in human exposure to radiofrequency radiation in excess of the applicable safety standards specified in § 1.1307(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes clarify wireless facility construction exclusions (e.g., mounting antennas on existing structures generally excluded unless §1.1307(a)(4) applies), encourage use of existing structures/corridors, and explain that specific size/height alone is generally not sufficient to trigger environmental processing except as required by § 1.1307/1.1308.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities that may require Environmental Assessments (EA) (§1.1307(a)(1)-(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission actions with respect to the following types of facilities may significantly affect the environment and thus require the preparation of EAs by the applicant: (1) Facilities to be located in an officially designated wilderness area; (2) Facilities to be located in an officially designated wildlife preserve; (3) Facilities that (i) may affect listed threatened or endangered species or designated critical habitats; or (ii) are likely to jeopardize the continued existence of any proposed endangered or threatened species or likely to result in the destruction or adverse modification of proposed critical habitats; (4) Facilities that may affect districts, sites, buildings, structures or objects significant in American history, architecture, archeology, engineering or culture that are listed or eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places and that are subject to review pursuant to section 1.1320 and have been determined through that review process to have adverse effects on identified historic properties; (5) Facilities that may affect Indian religious sites; (6) Facilities to be located in floodplains, if the facilities will not be placed at least one foot above the base flood elevation; (7) Facilities whose construction will involve significant change in surface features (e.g., wetland fill, deforestation or water diversion); (8) Antenna towers/supporting structures to be equipped with high intensity white lights located in residential neighborhoods, as defined by applicable zoning law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EAs may trigger further environmental processing (see §§1.1314, 1.1315, 1.1317); applicants should consult §1.1311 and §1.1308 for additional processing and application form guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: RF exposure compliance options for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to the limits on human exposure to RF provided in § 1.1310 of this chapter, applicants to the Commission for the grant or modification of construction permits, licenses or renewals thereof, temporary authorities, equipment authorizations, or any other authorizations for radiofrequency sources must either: (A) Determine that they qualify for an exemption pursuant to § 1.1307(b)(3); (B) Prepare an evaluation of the human exposure to RF radiation pursuant to § 1.1310 and include in the application a statement confirming compliance with the limits in § 1.1310; or (C) Prepare an Environmental Assessment if those RF sources would cause human exposure to levels of RF radiation in excess of the limits in § 1.1310.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance may be accomplished by mitigation actions per § 1.1307(b)(4). Upon request, the party must electronically submit technical information showing the basis for compliance. Exemptions/evaluations do not suffice where RF sources cause exposures in excess of §1.1310 limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to RF exposure determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Key definitions used in RF exposure evaluation include: Available maximum time-averaged power; Category One (spatial region compliant with general population exposure limit with continuous exposure or source-based time-averaged exposure); Category Two (general population limit exceeded but compliant with occupational exposure limit with continuous exposure); Category Three (occupational exposure limit exceeded but by no more than ten times); Category Four (exposure more than ten times occupational limit or possibility of serious injury on contact); Continuous exposure; Effective Radiated Power (ERP); Exemption (from routine environmental evaluation to demonstrate compliance with §1.1310, not an exemption from equipment authorization procedures or compliance obligations); Fixed RF source; Mobile device; Plane-wave equivalent power density; Portable device; Positive access control; Radiating structure; RF source; Separation distance; Source-based time averaging; Time-averaging period; Transient individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions establish spatial regions, averaging rules, mitigation triggers, and measurement concepts used throughout the RF evaluation and exemption criteria (e.g., time-averaging period not to exceed 30 minutes for fixed RF sources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of exemption for single RF sources (§1.1307(b)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For single RF sources (any single fixed RF source, mobile device, or portable device): A single RF source is exempt if: (A) The available maximum time-averaged power is no more than 1 mW, regardless of separation distance (medical implant devices may only use this exemption and the 1 mW in paragraph (b)(3)(i)(A)); or (B) The available maximum time-averaged power or effective radiated power (ERP), whichever is greater, is less than or equal to the threshold P_th (mW) described in the specified formula (usable at separation distances from 0.5 cm to 40 cm and frequencies 0.3 GHz to 6 GHz); or (C) Using Table 1 and the minimum separation distance (R in meters) from the body of a nearby person for the frequency (f in MHz) at which the source operates, the ERP (watts) is no more than the calculated value prescribed for that frequency. For the exemption in Table 1 to apply, R must be at least λ/2π. If ERP not easily obtained, available maximum power may be used if radiating structure dimensions or antenna gain criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 provides threshold ERP formulas by frequency ranges; the P_th formula and Table 1 methods are only applicable within specified separation distance and frequency ranges; medical implants have restricted allowance; physical antenna/structure constraints affect which metric may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of exemption for multiple RF sources (§1.1307(b)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple RF sources are exempt if: (A) The available maximum time-averaged power of each source is no more than 1 mW and there is a separation distance of two centimeters between any portion of a radiating structure operating and the nearest portion of any other radiating structure in the same device, except if the sum of multiple sources is less than 1 mW during the time-averaging period, in which case they may be treated as a single source; or (B) In the case of fixed RF sources operating in the same time-averaging period, or of multiple mobile or portable RF sources within a device operating in the same time averaging period, if the sum of the fractional contributions to the applicable thresholds is less than or equal to 1 as indicated in the specified equation (with variables a, b, c, P_i, P_th,i, ERP_j, ERP_th,j, Evaluated_k, Exposure Limit_k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The multi-source fractional-sum method requires calculating each source's contribution relative to exemption thresholds and summing; separation requirements and device-specific conditions apply; guidance lists variables and how to treat evaluated sources and existing transmitters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation measures for fixed RF sources (§1.1307(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific mitigation actions are required for fixed RF sources to the extent necessary to ensure compliance with exposure limits, including the implementation of an RF safety plan, restriction of access to those RF sources, and disclosure of spatial regions where exposure limits are exceeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation is tiered by Category: Category One (INFORMATION) — no mitigation required but optionally a green 'INFORMATION' sign with specified components; Category Two (NOTICE) — signs and positive access control required at the boundary where continuous exposure limit for general population is exceeded, appropriate signal word 'NOTICE' and color (blue), sign components per paragraph (b)(4)(vi); controlled conditions (e.g., limited-access rooftop) may permit attaching sign to antenna if it specifies minimum approach distance and is readable; occupational personnel must receive appropriate training and transient individuals must be supervised by trained personnel when entering controlled areas.
